title: POSSIBLE INCOMPLETE FIX of ledger M-01 — migrateIn slice ordering reaches the linear-depletion rate-drift class through the migration path
description: On NFTStakerDepletion `rate = budget / windowSeconds` is INDEPENDENT of `totalStaked`, so slice-1 users split the ENTIRE pool-wide emission stream among themselves while later slices sit parked. This is the phlimbo-ea Linear-Depletion class and the run-18 M-01 class, reached via the MIGRATION path. story-020 fixed the `unstake` path, not this one.
impact: Value transfer between users out of a shared reward budget. On NFTStakerDepletion the emission rate = budget / windowSeconds is INDEPENDENT of totalStaked, so slice-1 users split the ENTIRE pool-wide emission stream among themselves while every later slice sits parked in the migrator earning nothing. Measured: slice-1 user receives 120% of the slice-2 user (48,977.29e18 vs 40,758.11e18) over identical wall-clock exposure.
attackPath: 1. Operator calls finalizeAndReset (requires totalStaked == 0), which drains the depletion pool.
2. Emissions resume the instant slice 1 is re-injected via migrateIn -> depositFor.
3. Because rate is independent of totalStaked, the handful of slice-1 users receive the FULL pool-wide stream rather than their pro-rata share.
4. Slice-N users remain in the migrator's custody, accruing nothing, while their share of the shared rewardBudget is consumed.
5. Payout is decided entirely by which slice the operator assigned a user to — a variable no user controls and none can observe in advance.
likelihood: certain on any staggered migration of this contract. No attacker; the operator's ordinary slice ordering is the trigger. A clean remedy exists (setTargetAPY(0) immediately after finalizeAndReset, restore after the last slice) but it is not currently a documented runbook step.
assumptions: The migration is executed in more than one slice, which is the expected shape (ECON_C measures ~426 users per 30M-gas block, so multi-slice is required above that).
justification: Classified MEDIUM, matching ledger M-01's prior severity, under the standing rule that a finding of the same root-cause class reappearing after a `fixed` disposition inherits at least its prior severity. Project law ranks a possible incomplete fix second only to a REGRESSION precisely because 'an incomplete fix is more dangerous than an unfixed bug, because it reads as done'. story-020 closed the `unstake` path; the identical linear-depletion drift class reaches users through the untouched `migrateIn`/`depositFor` path. On the merits alone it is also Medium under C4: a value leak between users with stated assumptions and external requirements, PoC-measured at 120%. The dedup record pre-authorised a `medium` severityCeiling, so this is within band and not an overreach.

disputeFlag.evidenceForReopen: PoC_EconMigrateReady test_ECON_G — 120% on NFTStakerDepletion via operator-chosen migrateIn slice ordering. Same class as run-18 M-01 and the phlimbo-ea Linear-Depletion class. story-020 fixed the unstake path, not this one. Corroborating magnitudes on adjacent surfaces: 1000 bps on the price-scaled copy (test_ECON_A) and 1666 bps self-advancing (test_ECON_H).
disputeFlag.evidenceAgainstReopen: run-18 M-01 was AUTOMATIC drift on ordinary permissionless `unstake`. This is OPERATOR-CHOSEN slice ordering during a migration the operator controls, with a clean remedy (setTargetAPY(0) immediately after finalizeAndReset, restore after the last slice).
disputeFlag.myWeighing: The counter-argument bears on WHO triggers it, not on WHETHER the class is closed. Operator-controlled means the remedy is cheap and the trigger is predictable — it does not mean users are unharmed, and the harmed users have no agency at all. Combined with the incomplete-fix ranking, Medium is the honest floor. I record this as my reasoning, not as a settlement: a human must pick between `reopen b58b172e…` and `separate Medium`.
